column1: # Setting patches (dm/games/README.md, Setting patches): words of the game's code the host writes at launch when a setting has a value, each after checking the original word on the build it was found in.
# Shadows (static analysis of main e25c90c1… / v458752, checked against the rewriter's main.changed.tsv: no word is one the rewriter changed; README.md, Shadow settings)
# Shadow resolution: the per-frame shadow size (main+0x8186c) scales the preset size by max(renderW / 1920, renderH / 1080); fcsel s0,s0,s1,gt -> fmov s0,#1.0 keeps the full preset size
# Shadow map size: the quality presets built at stage start (main+0x6edda4) all ask for 2048: mov w26,#0x800 (Console, Handheld) and movk x26,#0x800,lsl #32 (UltraQuality, HighQuality)
# Upscale rate: fixed, or dynamic between a sharpest and a softest rate (static analysis of main e25c90c1… / v458752; README.md, Resolution model). The scene renders at the
# upscaler's output / the current rate, the rate state's +0xc ([[ctrl+0xf0]+0x270]; its only writers: the dynamic-resolution controller's store at main+0x38df0c and the parameter
# apply main+0x1605320, a vtable method agl calls whenever the graphics parameters are read). The controller (main+0x38db98, each frame) takes a scene entry's own rate (+0x2c) when
# the entry is not dynamic, else steps among the rates of a table built at run time (count <= 9; 1.0 no upscaler, 1.375, 12/7, 2.0 seen): toward softer up to NdsrUpscaleMaxRate
# (2.0) when over budget, toward sharper while above NdsrUpscaleMinRate (1.375), and stores the result snapped down to a table rate. Rate 1.0 turns its upscaler and mip bias off
# DM_UPSCALE_RATIO R, fixed (DM_UPSCALE_DYNAMIC unset or not 1): every frame takes the fixed-rate path (tbz w8,#1 -> b main+0x38de6c) with fmov s8,#R, the store takes R past
# the snap (main+0x38df08), and so does the parameter apply (main+0x16053a4). Only fmov immediates: Balanced is 1.6875 (27/16), not 1.7
# DM_UPSCALE_RATIO R with DM_UPSCALE_DYNAMIC=1, R the sharpest: as shipped the controller never lifts a rate below its min (it only refuses to step past it), a non-dynamic entry
# stores its own rate (1.0: native, no upscaler) and the store snaps R down to a table rate, so a stage could run sharper than R, at 1.0 with MetalFX off, until a slow frame.
# Instead the rate is clamped where every path joins (main+0x38de2c -> a clamp in the snap loop, dead once the store skips it): s8 = max(s8, R), then min(s8, softest)
# when DM_UPSCALE_SOFTEST has rows, and the store takes s8 itself (fmov s0,s8 at main+0x38dea4, b past the snap at main+0x38deb8). The controller's min rate becomes 1.0 and its
# max 2.0 (its four reads), so it still steps through all of its own rates and the clamp maps them into the range; the parameter apply starts each stage at R.
# Ultra performance (3.0, a rate the game never chooses) is fixed only, and only with DM_UPSCALER metalfx or metalfx-temporal: agl's network was never run that far
# DM_UPSCALE_SOFTEST F, the softest rate with dynamic resolution (DM_UPSCALE_DYNAMIC=1 and a DM_UPSCALE_RATIO from 1.0 to 2.0, or native-mfx (1.0), written first: the when terms on DM_UPSCALE_RATIO
# test what that variable wrote): the clamp's min(s8, F) (two words of the dead snap loop, which run as harmless integer moves without it) and the step to softer's last
# resort (main+0x38e278 fmov s2,s4, the current rate when no table rate is left below its max) -> fmov s2,#F, so the controller can reach a softest rate past its table.
# A softest rate sharper than the sharpest is raised to it (its own rows per sharpest), and Ultra performance without a MetalFX upscaler is lowered to Performance; unset, the

# stores table index 0 and NDSR's execute (main+0x325a80) then runs only its SMAA into the output; four words in the function's floor of the width (a branch for negative

column1: # Frame rate mode (README.md, Frame rate mode): the frame-rate controller main+0x204a18 (once a frame from main+0x203718 while VRR is off) turns the frame's measure (frame start to the later
# of its submission and the GPU's end, v vsyncs) into a target interval trunc(v - 0.2) + 1 (main+0x204ab0), clamps it to [min, max] (main+0x204ab8-0x204ac4), steps up after 2 frames above the
# interval and down one step after its countdown (+0x4c, 6, decremented only on frames below the interval: main+0x204b00-0x204b10) unless a listener vetoes (main+0x204b90). The game advances a
# fixed step of its interval per frame (sead's vsync wait main+0x1578e94 and the frame deadline main+0x5c62e4 read it), so a frame slower than its interval runs the game slow: the step-up
# path stays the game's own in both values, and the game's speed with it.
# Prefer 60 breaks the 30 fps trap (the GPU and CPU clocks follow the longer interval, so the measure stays above 1.2 vsyncs and the countdown never runs): after a step up the countdown is 120
# frames (main+0x204bc4 ldr w12,[x20,#0x10] -> mov w12,#120) and runs on every frame, halving on frames below the interval (main+0x204b04-0x204b0c: lsr w8,w11,#1; sub w12,w11,#1;
# csel w8,w8,w12,lt), so a light scene steps down after 7 frames as before and any scene tries 60 again after 120 frames (4 s at 30 fps); the veto is skipped (cbnz -> nop).
# Hold 30 raises the clamp's lower bound to 2 (main+0x204a88 add + main+0x204a8c ldr -> ldr x8,[x8,#0xfd0] + mov w12,#2; main+0x204ac0 / 0x204ac4 compare and select w12 instead of the
# controller's min): never 60, 20 when a frame needs it
